assign.now: cause found - fs.watch handles on DELETED directories spin forever

log.msg: CPU baseline. My own PORT=8092 server (pid 21872) idled at 0.0-2.9% for its first nine minutes. Three older servers started by other minions sat at 119-129% the whole time. Per-thread sampling on two of them: ONE thread at 100% (the main JS thread) plus four threadpool threads at 3-6% each.

watchspy sees almost nothing. A fresh chokidar with the server's exact options over the same tree reported 0-7 raw events/s (73 in 10s), nearly all of them the servers' own directory.json writes. So the flood is NOT arriving from the filesystem at large - a NEW watcher never sees it. That is why five earlier investigations could not name it.

Reproduced on demand. I churned 12 directories under my own task dir (mkdir + a file, 400ms, rm -rf, 400ms). My server went 2.9% -> 13% -> 134% and stayed there after the churn stopped. Memory 224MB -> 425MB.

Profile of MY spinning server (pid 21872, 5s, 3259 samples), inclusive time: 36% FSWatcher._handle.onchange -> 36% chokidar handleEvent -> 23% fsWatchBroadcast -> 33% _handleRead -> 19% path.join, 8% readdirp, 4% handleErrorFromBinding (readdir of a vanished dir). Identical to the 2026-08-19 profile in Server/doc/spin.md.

THE CAUSE, named. Probing the live process through its own inspector (process._getActiveHandles + a hook on each FSWatcher's onchange) counted 191,058 change events in 5 seconds - 38,212 events per second - and SIX handles produced 31,842-31,843 of them each. All six are directories I had already deleted: public/framework/ai/2026-09-06/server-spin/churn/d0 d1 d2 d4 d9 d11. On Windows an fs.watch handle whose directory is deleted underneath it fires change events in a tight loop forever, at ~6,400/s per handle, and chokidar never closes it. Six stranded handles = 38k events/s = a pinned core.

Everything the doc could not explain follows from that: a fresh watcher (watchspy) sees nothing because it never watched the vanished dir; the source dies with the process because the handle does; it comes back every few days because that is how often something deletes a directory under public/ while the server runs; and it is doubled because Directory.js and LiveReload.js each open their own chokidar over the same 1865 dirs - 8,532 FSWatcher handles in one process.

assign.now: fixed and proved - one recursive fs.watch handle replaces 8,532

log.msg: THE FIX. New Server/watch.js: ONE recursive fs.watch handle on public/ itself, shared by both consumers. public/ is never deleted, so no handle can ever be stranded - the whole class is gone, not just today's instance. Directory.js and LiveReload.js both subscribe; chokidar is gone from Server/. Windows reports create/delete/rename as 'rename' and a write into an existing file as 'change', which is exactly the split the two consumers needed: Directory rebuilds directory.json only on 'rename' (a 'change' leaves it byte-identical and the rebuild costs 110ms of blocking walk), LiveReload takes both. Directory's guard also became a proper trailing debounce with a 1s ceiling - the old leading guard dropped every event that arrived during the 110ms walk.

CPU before -> after, same box, same tree, same reproducer. BEFORE: 12 create/delete dir cycles took my server from 2.9% to 134% and it stayed there. AFTER: the same 12 cycles leave it at 1.1%, and 20 cycles at 1.9%. Idle: 134% -> 0.1%. fs.watch handles: 8,532 -> 1 (process handles 8,726 -> 260). Memory: 224-480MB -> 125MB. Side by side right now: four servers still on the old code sit at 118-122% with ~8,850 handles each; mine sits at 0.1-5.7% with 260.

All four jobs still work, measured on the fixed server (scratchpad/server-spin/prove.mjs, run three times): an edit under public/ reloads in 313-326ms with the exact path on the wire; a new directory reaches directory.json and is announced in 542-568ms; a line appended to ai/2026-09-06/server-spin/task.jsonl reaches a subscribed socket in 1-2ms; /framework/ serves 200 text/html. Bonus: renaming a directory under public/ no longer fails with EPERM.

Honest residual. Rebuilding directory.json is now the server's biggest cost - 110ms of blocking walk per structural change, 69 rebuilds in 221s while six agents were writing files, which is why the same server reads 0.1% alone and about 5% under today's load. Making it incremental is the next win and a bigger change than this one; noted in doc/spin.md with the measurement that would guide it.

Out of my fence, named so it is one minute to fix: three mentions of chokidar in public/framework/dev/ are now stale (page.js:30, doc/decisions.md:13, Socket/doc/wire.md:307). chokidar stays in package.json - the fans skill's watchspy.mjs loads it from node_modules.

assign.outcome:
**The spin is named and fixed. A fresh dev server idles at 0.1% instead of 134%.**

**The cause.** On Windows an `fs.watch` handle whose directory is *deleted underneath it* never closes and never goes quiet - it fires `change` events in a tight loop, for ever, at ~6,400 a second. chokidar opened one such handle for every one of the 1,865 directories under `public/`, twice over (`Directory.js` and `LiveReload.js` each ran their own). Delete a directory under `public/` while the server runs and that handle is stranded until the process dies.

**Measured, not reasoned.** 12 create/delete dir cycles took my own server from 2.9% to 134%, permanently. Hooking every `FSWatcher.onchange` inside that live process counted **191,058 events in 5 s = 38,212/s**, of which six handles produced 31,842 each - all six watching directories that were already deleted. That is why five earlier hunts failed: `watchspy.mjs` starts a *fresh* chokidar, which never watched the vanished dir, so it read 0-7 events/s beside servers burning 120%.

**The fix** - `Server/watch.js`: **one** recursive `fs.watch` handle on `public/` itself, shared by both consumers. `public/` is never deleted, so nothing can be stranded - the class is gone, not just today's instance. chokidar is out of `Server/`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 134% after 12 dir deletions, permanently | **0.1%** idle, 1.9% after 20 |
| `fs.watch` handles | 8,532 | **1** (260 process handles, was 8,726) |
| memory | 224 -> 480 MB | 125 MB |

Four servers still on the old code sit at 118-122% beside mine right now.

**All four jobs still work**, run three times: an edit under `public/` reloads in **313-326 ms**; a new directory reaches `directory.json` in **542-568 ms**; an appended `task.jsonl` line reaches a subscriber in **1-2 ms**; `/framework/` serves 200. Bonus: renaming a directory under `public/` no longer fails with `EPERM`.

**The owner must restart their server** - the fix arrives no other way.

Files: `Server/watch.js` (new) - `Server/plugins/Directory.js` - `Server/plugins/SocketServer/LiveReload.js` - `Server/doc/spin.md` (rewritten: the cause, the numbers, what is left) - `Server/README.md`.

**Left, with reasons.** Rebuilding `directory.json` is now the top cost - 110 ms of blocking walk per structural change, which is why the same server reads 0.1% alone and ~5% while six agents write files; making it incremental is a bigger change than this one and wants its own task (`doc/spin.md` carries the measurement that would guide it). Three stale mentions of chokidar in `public/framework/dev/` are outside my write fence, named to the line. `ai/usage.json` not refreshed - outside my fence.
